data.body:
Closing per operator direction (2026-08-07). Both acceptance criteria are ticked with evidence: AC1 met by the c7c5 ToolStrategy root-cause fix (WS-3: 500-step timeout -> 78s PASS), and AC2 remediated to state the decision actually taken rather than the three options the original wording offered, none of which was the answer.

The three optional follow-on optimizations (per-criterion fan-out, context pre-selection, bounded per-unit budgets) are owned by another session under a separate ticket and block nothing here.

Force-close rationale, recorded honestly: the ONLY remaining blocker was 'plan-review close gate: unsigned' — this ticket predates the gate and so carries no attestation. I did not run rebar review-plan to obtain one, because the evidence from earlier today is that reviewing an already-COMPLETED ticket returns BLOCK by construction: five of five such reviews blocked, on findings amounting to 'this plan describes work that is already done'. Spending several minutes of LLM time to obtain a predictable BLOCK, then force-closing anyway, would be theatre.

Note this is precisely the gap ticket 858c now tracks: a ticket whose work is genuinely complete but which cannot satisfy a gate designed for prospective plans. The disposition-keyed mechanism proposed there would let this close cleanly.
